title: Symfony Quick Reference
description: Look up a lesson idea, see its small example, and check a common mistake. Open the linked lesson for setup and practice steps.

entries.name: Make a controller route
entries.summary: A Route attribute maps a URL to a controller method. Open GET /hello.

example.code:
<?php
namespace App\Controller;
use Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\Controller\AbstractController;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\JsonResponse;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RedirectResponse;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;
class LessonController extends AbstractController {
#[Route("/hello", methods: ["GET"])]
public function hello(): Response { return new Response("Hello, Asha!"); }
}

notes: Keep the attribute above the method it describes.

entries.name: Return JSON data
entries.summary: JsonResponse turns an array into JSON and sets its content type. Open GET /book.

example.code:
<?php
namespace App\Controller;
use Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\Controller\AbstractController;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\JsonResponse;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RedirectResponse;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;
class LessonController extends AbstractController {
#[Route("/book", methods: ["GET"])]
public function book(): JsonResponse { return new JsonResponse(["title" => "Moon Trip", "pages" => 24]); }
}

notes: Use JsonResponse rather than hand-building JSON strings.

entries.name: Read a route value
entries.summary: A route placeholder can become a method input. Open GET /hello/Ravi.

example.code:
<?php
namespace App\Controller;
use Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\Controller\AbstractController;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\JsonResponse;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RedirectResponse;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;
class LessonController extends AbstractController {
#[Route("/hello/{name}", methods: ["GET"])]
public function hello(string $name): Response { return new Response("Hi, " . $name . "!", 200, ["Content-Type" => "text/plain"]); }
}

notes: Treat route inputs as untrusted text.

entries.name: Read query data
entries.summary: A Request object gives access to query values. Open GET /search?q=cat.

example.code:
<?php
namespace App\Controller;
use Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\Controller\AbstractController;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\JsonResponse;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RedirectResponse;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;
class LessonController extends AbstractController {
#[Route("/search", methods: ["GET"])]
public function search(Request $request): JsonResponse { return new JsonResponse(["term" => $request->query->get("q", "")]); }
}

notes: Check client values before using them in a database query or file path.

entries.name: Constrain a path number
entries.summary: A route requirement describes allowed path text. Open GET /double/4.

example.code:
<?php
namespace App\Controller;
use Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\Controller\AbstractController;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\JsonResponse;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RedirectResponse;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;
class LessonController extends AbstractController {
#[Route("/double/{n}", requirements: ["n" => "[0-9]+"], methods: ["GET"])]
public function twice(int $n): JsonResponse { return new JsonResponse(["answer" => $n * 2]); }
}

notes: A requirement controls route matching, not every allowed data range.

entries.name: Read a JSON body
entries.summary: Request::toArray reads JSON into an array. Send POST /books with application/json and {"title":"Moon Trip"}.

example.code:
<?php
namespace App\Controller;
use Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\Controller\AbstractController;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\JsonResponse;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RedirectResponse;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;
class LessonController extends AbstractController {
#[Route("/books", methods: ["POST"])]
public function create(Request $request): JsonResponse {
 $data = $request->toArray();
 if (!is_string($data["title"] ?? null)) return new JsonResponse(["error" => "Title needed"], 400);
 return new JsonResponse(["title" => $data["title"]], 201);
}
}

notes: Malformed JSON can fail before your own field checks run.

entries.name: Generate a named URL
entries.summary: A route name lets code build a link without repeating its path. Open GET /link.

example.code:
<?php
namespace App\Controller;
use Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\Controller\AbstractController;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\JsonResponse;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RedirectResponse;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;
class LessonController extends AbstractController {
#[Route("/hello/{name}", name: "hello", methods: ["GET"])]
public function hello(string $name): Response { return new Response($name); }
#[Route("/link", methods: ["GET"])]
public function link(): Response { return new Response($this->generateUrl("hello", ["name" => "Asha"])); }
}

notes: The parameter key must match the placeholder.

entries.name: Return a redirect
entries.summary: RedirectResponse tells a client where to request next. GET /start ends at /hello in a browser.

example.code:
<?php
namespace App\Controller;
use Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\Controller\AbstractController;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\JsonResponse;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RedirectResponse;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;
class LessonController extends AbstractController {
#[Route("/start", methods: ["GET"])]
public function start(): RedirectResponse { return new RedirectResponse("/hello"); }
#[Route("/hello", methods: ["GET"])]
public function hello(): Response { return new Response("Welcome"); }
}

notes: A redirect starts a new client request.

entries.name: Send an error status
entries.summary: The second JsonResponse argument is the status. Open GET /missing.

example.code:
<?php
namespace App\Controller;
use Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\Controller\AbstractController;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\JsonResponse;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RedirectResponse;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;
class LessonController extends AbstractController {
#[Route("/missing", methods: ["GET"])]
public function missing(): JsonResponse { return new JsonResponse(["error" => "Book not found"], 404); }
}

notes: Do not hide a missing item behind a 200 success status.

entries.name: Add reply metadata
entries.summary: A Response has a header bag. Open GET /note and inspect Cache-Control.

example.code:
<?php
namespace App\Controller;
use Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\Controller\AbstractController;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\JsonResponse;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RedirectResponse;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;
class LessonController extends AbstractController {
#[Route("/note", methods: ["GET"])]
public function note(): Response { $response = new Response("Practice note"); $response->headers->set("Cache-Control", "no-store"); return $response; }
}

notes: Headers and body are separate parts of a response.

entries.name: Restrict an HTTP method
entries.summary: The methods option limits which requests match. GET /ready gives this reply; POST is not allowed.

example.code:
<?php
namespace App\Controller;
use Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\Controller\AbstractController;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\JsonResponse;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RedirectResponse;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;
class LessonController extends AbstractController {
#[Route("/ready", methods: ["GET"])]
public function ready(): Response { return new Response("Ready"); }
}

notes: Use the correct HTTP method for the operation.

entries.name: Send a list of values
entries.summary: A PHP list becomes a JSON array. Open GET /books.

example.code:
<?php
namespace App\Controller;
use Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\Controller\AbstractController;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\JsonResponse;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RedirectResponse;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;
class LessonController extends AbstractController {
#[Route("/books", methods: ["GET"])]
public function books(): JsonResponse { return new JsonResponse(["Moon Trip", "Sun Trip"]); }
}

notes: A JSON list has ordered items; an object has named fields.
